course.title: C
course.description: A complete, research-based C course progressing from the language and compilation model through pointers, memory ownership, data modeling, multi-file builds, I/O, debugging, testing, concurrency, secure coding, portability, and a realistic final project. It uses C23 as the current standard reference while emphasizing durable C11/C17 concepts used in existing codebases.
prerequisites: Basic computer literacy and terminal/IDE use.
No prior programming language is required.
learningOutcomes: Compile C with an explicit standard and strong diagnostics.
Use core C types, control flow, functions, arrays, pointers, strings, structs, enums, and unions correctly.
Design safe dynamic-memory ownership and lifetime contracts.
Build multi-file C projects with CMake.
Implement robust file and command-line I/O with validation and error handling.
Diagnose memory errors and undefined behavior with gdb, sanitizers, and Memcheck.
Reason about C11 threading, mutexes, atomics, and synchronization.
Apply defensive coding practices for bounds, integer arithmetic, parsing, and resource cleanup.
Deliver a tested, maintainable C application with a reproducible build.

tasks.title: Safe line-oriented file copier
tasks.description: Copy a file using bounded buffers and checked stdio operations.
tasks.problemStatement: Handle partial writes, read errors, and close failures.
tasks.hint: fwrite can write fewer bytes than requested.
tasks.solutionCode: FILE*in=fopen(src,"rb");FILE*out=fopen(dst,"wb");unsigned char b[8192];size_t n;int ok=in&&out;while(ok&&(n=fread(b,1,sizeof b,in))){size_t o=0;while(o<n){size_t w=fwrite(b+o,1,n-o,out);if(!w){ok=0;break;}o+=w;}}if(in&&ferror(in))ok=0;if(in)fclose(in);if(out&&fclose(out)!=0)ok=0;return ok?0:1;
tasks.solutionExplanation: The solution treats I/O as fallible and handles partial writes.

tasks.title: Defensive packet parser
tasks.description: Parse a small binary header without assuming alignment, padding, or host byte order.
tasks.problemStatement: Reject short buffers, unsupported versions, and payload lengths larger than available data.
tasks.hint: Read bytes and assemble integers with shifts.
tasks.solutionCode:
static uint16_t be16(const uint8_t*p){return (uint16_t)(((uint16_t)p[0]<<8)|p[1]);}
int parse(const uint8_t*b,size_t n,uint8_t*v,uint16_t*plen){if(!b||!v||!plen||n<4)return 0;*v=b[0];if(*v!=1)return 0;uint16_t p=be16(b+2);if((size_t)p>n-4)return 0;*plen=p;return 1;}
tasks.solutionExplanation: The parser validates length before reading and defines endianness explicitly.

project.name: Secure Log Indexer
project.description: A modular C command-line application that parses newline-delimited records, validates input, stores records in an owned growable index, summarizes severity, and is built/tested with CMake and sanitizers. It is intentionally framework-free so the student practices the language and standard library directly.
steps: Create include/, src/, tests/, and build/ directories.
Implement log parsing with two delimiters and strict severity validation.
Duplicate timestamp/message strings so the store owns their lifetime.
Grow LogStore with realloc using overflow checks and a temporary pointer.
Read files with fgets into a bounded buffer and reject detected overlong records.
Count records by severity and print a summary.
Add assertions covering valid parsing, invalid severity, and store growth.
Build and test with CMake, then run sanitizer-enabled builds.
Audit every allocation and file handle for one clear cleanup path.

code.CMakeLists.txt:
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.20)
project(logindexer C)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_C_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF)
add_library(logcore src/log.c)
target_include_directories(logcore PUBLIC ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include)
target_compile_options(logcore PRIVATE -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
add_executable(logindexer src/main.c)
target_link_libraries(logindexer PRIVATE logcore)
add_executable(log_tests tests/test_log.c)
target_link_libraries(log_tests PRIVATE logcore)
enable_testing()
add_test(NAME log_tests COMMAND log_tests)

project.explanation: The library owns each stored record and its strings. Parsing allocates independent copies, log_store_push transfers ownership into the growable array, and destruction frees every owned string exactly once. The CLI treats input as untrusted, bounds each line, checks parsing and allocation failures, and releases the file/store on every path. Tests cover valid parsing, invalid severity, dynamic growth, and counting. CMake provides a reproducible target graph. Development builds should use warnings and sanitizers; release builds should not ship sanitizer runtimes merely because they were used for testing.
